title: Span + Waterfall + Filter Prototyping notes
content:
Context and objective:
This doc collects rapid UX sketches, interaction notes, and grooming items for the Request Tracing surface we want to ship in Console 2.0. Target audience: engineers and SREs who need to debug high-latency requests and see span-level timings for inference requests across the serving stack (frontend router, batching layer, model workers, cache hits).

Primary goals (succinct):
- Surface a timeline (waterfall) view of spans for a single request and for aggregated requests.
- Enable fast filtering and drilldown (by route, model, host, GPU type, latency bucket, user id).
- Make common debugging workflows 3 clicks or less (find slowest span, jump to logs/traces, open raw request payload).
- Support grouping/aggregation of spans to reduce noise for golden-path requests.

High-level constraints:
- Must render thousands of spans in aggregate view with client-side virtualization.
- Keep initial load fast (server returns minimal span summary; expand on demand).
- Reuse existing Console style tokens and table components where possible.

Quick persona scenarios:
- Oncall SRE: sees a rise in 95th percentile latency; wants to find if batching or KV cache is the cause.
- ML infra engineer: validating a new kernel selection rollout; wants to compare waterfall shapes between two model variants.
- Product engineer: investigating an error spike correlated with a recent rollout; wants to filter to requests that experienced fallback to smaller model.

Wireframe sketch (textual):
Top bar: date range selector | environment selector (prod/staging) | quick search (free text)
Left column (narrow): filter builder (pills + typed query) + saved filters list + histogram of request counts by minute
Main pane (split vertically):
  A) Request list (top half): table with columns [timestamp, request-id, route, model, total-latency, status, max-span] + action menu (open trace, export, annotate)
  B) Waterfall viewer (bottom half, resizable): timeline with spans stacked vertically, color-coded by span type (router, batcher, kv-cache, model-infer, grpc, io), with a horizontal scale bar and hover tooltips showing start/end/duration and metadata (host, GPU, batch-size).
Right flyout (contextual, opens on span click): span details, logs tail, raw request/response, related traces (similar request-ids), link to trace in external APM if present.

Key interactions and microflows:
1) Quick-find slow requests:
   - Type ">200ms" in quick search or select 95th percentile bucket in histogram -> list filters to matching requests -> waterfall auto-scrolls to selected request -> first visible span is highlighted and badge shows "slowest span".
2) Compare two traces side-by-side:
   - Select checkbox next to two requests -> click "Compare" -> open split-view waterfall with aligned request start times and per-span diff overlays (delta labels).
3) Aggregate view by span name:
   - Toggle "Aggregate" -> group spans by canonical operation name (e.g., "kv:get"), show aggregated bar with min/avg/p95 and sample spans. Clicking group expands to sample traces.
4) Keyboard support:
   - Up/Down to move between requests; Right arrow to expand waterfall; Enter to open span flyout; F to focus filter input.

Filter language / semantics (proposal):
- Support typed filter with simple grammar: field:value, comparisons for numeric fields (latency>200), relative time (last:30m), tag inclusion (tags:cache-hit), regex on route (route~"^/v1/.*").
- Provide auto-complete suggestions from recent values and schema.
- Saved filters exposed in left panel with star favorites.

Span grouping and naming hygiene notes:
- We must canonicalize span names at ingestion (router.resolve, batch.enqueue, batch.dispatch, kv.get, model.predict, grpc.send).
- Add a display-name mapping layer to collapse internal noise (e.g., multiple library-level spans into "batcher" group).
- Introduce tags for span: {component, host, batch_size, model_variant, quantization}. These are used for coloring and aggregation.

Waterfall visualization specifics:
- Time axis uses relative start-of-request as zero and shows absolute timestamps on hover.
- Spans draw as rounded bars; nested spans show indentation via y-axis; overlapping spans side-by-side with z-order determined by start time.
- Hover tooltip must show: span name, duration, start offset, node host, GPU type if present, any error code, link to logs.
- When clicking the left-most request column row, waterfall scrolls to and centers that request with a soft highlight.

Performance and data-loading strategy:
- Request list fetch returns minimal summary and a set of top-3 longest spans per request. Detailed spans fetched on waterfall demand or when expanding a request.
- For aggregate views, server returns pre-aggregated histogram and representative sample traces (one per bucket).
- Use streaming websocket to append new traces in real-time when live tail mode is enabled.

Edge cases and error states:
- Partial traces: show a "missing spans" badge and visualize what we have; provide link to raw logs as fallback.
- Extremely wide spans (>30s): collapse to 30s in UI but show actual value; allow expand to true scale.
- Cross-service time skew: detect and show clock-drift warning; offer option to align by client vs server time.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can filter request list by route, model, and latency and see waterfall for any selected request.
- Waterfall renders correct hierarchical spans for selected trace with metadata flyout.
- Aggregation toggle produces grouped spans with sample detail.
- Keyboard shortcuts for main navigation implemented.
- Unit + e2e tests for filter grammar and waterfall rendering of nested spans.

Backlog grooming (epics & estimated priority):
- Epic: Basic trace viewer (MVP) — priority: P0 — scope: request list, single-trace waterfall, span flyout (est: 6 sprints)
- Epic: Aggregation + compare view — priority: P1 — scope: grouped spans, compare two traces, sample extraction (est: 4 sprints)
- Epic: Live tailing and realtime alerts — priority: P2 — scope: websocket tail, alert linkouts (est: 3 sprints)
- Task: span name canonicalization mapping (infra + ingestion change) — priority: P0 — depends on ingestion team
- Task: color palette for span types + accessibility contrast checks — priority: P1
- Task: performance budget (render <200ms for 2000 spans) — priority: P0

Open questions (to resolve in grooming):
- Should we persist column sorting and layout per-user? (UX leaning: yes, but need storage plan)
- What RBAC restrictions required for showing raw request payload? (security to define allowed roles)
- How to represent fallback transitions (e.g., model A failed -> model B used) visually without clutter? (proposal: small connector arrow and note in span tooltip)
- Do we link to Redwood's rollout records when a trace coincides with a canary? (product: yes, helpful)

Next steps / short-term tasks before stakeholder review meeting:
- UX: create 3 quick clickable mockups (single-trace, aggregate, compare) using local components (owner: Sofia, due 2025-08-20).
- Eng: confirm ingestion changes for canonical span names and top-3 spans precompute (owner: Ethan, due 2025-08-25).
- Security: list of roles that can view raw payloads and suggested masking defaults (owner: Priya, due 2025-08-22).
- PM: create JIRA epic and link this doc (owner: Liam, due 2025-08-18).

Notes to self (drafty):
- Consider micro-interactions: on hover a subtle drop-shadow, quick-copy request-id, and "open replay" action for requests with recorded payloads.
- Think about onboarding tooltip for "Aggregate" toggle explaining it reduces noise by grouping identical spans.
- Keep default color for model-infer warm (orange) to draw attention in latency investigations.

End of notes.
